newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in London, Dow seen lower.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in London, Dow seen lower.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mixed in London on Monday in thin trading as European investors awaited a slew on results from U.S. blue chips due this week, dealers said.
"There are a few special situations, but it's very slow," said one dealer.
Activity could pick up later in the week with the release of U.S. retail sales and the consumer price index, but investors mostly were awaiting corporate results.
"This market is mainly earnings driven and there's no room for disappointment," said one dealer, who was expecting the Dow to open about five to seven points lower.

Shares in Waste Management Inc advanced $3/8 to $33-3/8 in London, buoyed by a story in the Wall Street Journal that said the company would announce the appointment of Ronald LeMay as new chairman and chief executive, ending a five-month search. LeMay is president and chief operating officer of Sprint Corp.
"It will lift the uncertainty and maybe (LeMay) will make some changes," the dealer said.
Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc eased $1/4 to $42-7/8 amid ongoing concerns the status of the industry tobacco deal, dealers said.
Shares in Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc fell $3/8 to $43-3/8 after a negative press comment on Barron's, dealers said.
Shares in Intel Corp, set to split today, were up $1/4 to 154 on a post-split basis. The computer chip manufacturer is scheduled to release its second quarter results on Tuesday.
Boeing Co shares climbed $1/4 to $56-3/4 as the U.S. increased pressure on the European Union to clear the planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp.
In other trading, September S&P 500 index futures were 0.15 point higher at 924.60 on Globex at 1023 GMT, while September long bond futures were down 3/32 at 114-1/32.
No U.S. economic data are due today.
